bill_text.text_with_changes:
A bill for an act relating to housing; providing additional accommodations to children with autism in rental properties; proposing coding for new law in Minnesota Statutes, chapter 504B.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1.

[+[504B.213] CHILDREN WITH AUTISM; PROTECTION IN RENTAL PROPERTY. +]

[+(a) A tenant who has a child with autism living with the tenant may request a reasonable accommodation to protect the child from harm when the tenant identifies a lake, river, stream, other body of water, or other attractive nuisance, that is accessible and in close proximity to the landlord's property. Upon such request, a landlord must make reasonable modifications to policies, practices, or procedures for the rental property, or make reasonable modifications to the property or facilities on the property, unless the modifications would fundamentally alter the nature of the facilities or other structural aspects of the property. +]

[+(b) A landlord may require documentation from a tenant that the child is autistic unless the child's condition is readily apparent or already known to the landlord. +]

[+(c) A landlord who receives or accommodates a request for a reasonable accommodation under this section may not retaliate in any way against the tenant. +]
bill_text.plain_text:
A bill for an act relating to housing; providing additional accommodations to children with autism in rental properties; proposing coding for new law in Minnesota Statutes, chapter 504B.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1.

[504B.213] CHILDREN WITH AUTISM; PROTECTION IN RENTAL PROPERTY.

(a) A tenant who has a child with autism living with the tenant may request a reasonable accommodation to protect the child from harm when the tenant identifies a lake, river, stream, other body of water, or other attractive nuisance, that is accessible and in close proximity to the landlord's property. Upon such request, a landlord must make reasonable modifications to policies, practices, or procedures for the rental property, or make reasonable modifications to the property or facilities on the property, unless the modifications would fundamentally alter the nature of the facilities or other structural aspects of the property.

(b) A landlord may require documentation from a tenant that the child is autistic unless the child's condition is readily apparent or already known to the landlord.

(c) A landlord who receives or accommodates a request for a reasonable accommodation under this section may not retaliate in any way against the tenant.
